G3-contract.need: Contract review against a standard, then a clause rewrite

turns.asked: Review the vendor's draft against our standard agreement. What is missing or worse for us?
turns.answer:
The vendor's draft diverges from your standard in nine places. I'll work through them clause by clause (standard vs draft), then flag what is missing or worse.

## Where the draft is worse than your standard

**Security — weakened, and dropped a required element**
- Standard requires encryption at rest *and* in transit "as required by Article 32 GDPR" [p1-s3]. The draft only promises measures the vendor "considers reasonable" [p1-s3]. This is open-ended and no longer tied to any legal standard — it removes the encryption obligation entirely.

**Sub-processors — materially worse**
- Standard: no sub-processor without **prior written notice of at least 30 days** plus your **right to object**, and the vendor stays **liable** for them [p1-s4].
- Draft: the vendor may engage sub-processors **at its discretion**, merely publishing a list on its website [p1-s4]. No notice, no right to object, no stated liability. This is the biggest downgrade.

**Breach notification — materially worse**
- Standard: "without undue delay and in any event within **48 hours** after **becoming aware**" [p1-s6].
- Draft: "**within 7 days after confirming** it" [p1-s6]. That is up to ~7× longer and adds a "confirming" precondition you can't verify, versus a fixed 48-hour clock.

**End-of-services — missing the return option, adds a delay**
- Standard: delete **or return** all Personal Data **at your choice** [p1-s7].
- Draft: only **deletion**, and **within 180 days** [p1-s7]. You lose the return option and accept a six-month tail during which your data stays on their systems.

**Governing law — worse for you**
- Standard: **Ireland** [p1-s9]. Draft: **Cayman Islands** [p1-s9]. This moves enforcement away from an EU jurisdiction and likely weakens your data-protection position.

**Data subject requests — added cost to you**
- Standard: assistance is provided, no cost stated [p1-s5]. Draft: assistance is "at the Controller's **cost**" [p1-s5]. You'd pay for compliance the vendor is already obligated to support.

## What is in the draft but missing from your standard (and adverse)

**New clause — use of your data**
- The draft adds a right for the vendor to "use **aggregated and de-identified** Customer Personal Data to **improve its products and for marketing**" [p1-s8]. This clause does not exist in your standard at all, and "de-identified for marketing" is a risk you should resist unless it is genuinely irreversible.

## What matches your standard (no issue)
- Purpose/term [p1-s0], documented instructions [p1-s1], confidentiality [p1-s2] are identical.

## Suggested asks before signing
1. Restore encryption at rest and in transit per Article 32 GDPR.
2. Bring back 30-day prior written sub-processor notice, your right to object, and vendor liability for sub-processors.
3. Cut breach notice back to 48 hours from awareness (no "confirming" condition).
4. Add the return option at your choice and shorten deletion from 180 days.
5. Move governing law back to Ireland.
6. Remove "at the Controller's cost" on data subject requests.
7. Delete or renegotiate the aggregated/de-identified data-use clause.

Want me to draft the redline language for any of these, or produce a side-by-side comparison table you can send back to the vendor?

turns.asked: Propose a rewrite of the breach notification clause in the vendor draft so it says 48 hours.
turns.answer:
Here's the proposed rewrite of the breach notification clause ([p1-s6]) in the vendor draft:

**Proposed (48-hour clock, no "confirming" condition):**
> The Processor notifies the Controller without undue delay and in any event within **48 hours** after **becoming aware** of a Personal Data Breach.

This matches your standard agreement ([p1-s6]) and removes two weaknesses from the draft:
- The **7-day** window is cut to **48 hours**.
- The "**after confirming** it" precondition is dropped in favour of "**after becoming aware**" — so the clock starts the moment the vendor knows, not when it has finished an internal confirmation you can't verify.

This is a preview (rewrite `01a1f805-3f87-72ca-a64a-5a4526e92e60`) and **nothing has been saved** — nothing changes until you accept it. Want me to also redline the other weaker clauses (sub-processors, security, end-of-services) in the same pass?

AAT103a-draft.need: Draft an observation from rough notes and test results

turns.asked: Draft the observation for test step T1 with these headings: condition, criteria, cause, effect, recommendation. Use only what is in the notes and the procedure, and after each statement cite the test step or the paragraph it comes from.
turns.answer:
## Test Step T1 — Observation

**Condition.** Test step T1 samples 25 new accounts against procedure 2.2 (Branch Operations Manager signature on application); 4 of the 25 had no Branch Operations Manager signature [p1-s1, fieldwork notes], on accounts AC-0007, AC-0019, AC-0033 and AC-0051 [p1-s1, fieldwork notes]. All 4 accounts were active [p1-s1, fieldwork notes].

**Criteria.** Procedure 2.2 requires the Branch Operations Manager to sign the application form before the account is activated, and states that an application without this signature must not be activated [p1-s2, account-opening procedure 2.2].

**Cause.** The branch manager says the sign-offs were missed because of the month-end rush, with two officers short in August [p1-s2, fieldwork notes]. The system also allows an account to be activated without the signature being scanned in, with no hard stop [p1-s2, fieldwork notes].

**Effect.** Accounts AC-0007, AC-0019, AC-0033 and AC-0051 were activated without the required Branch Operations Manager signature, contrary to procedure 2.2 [p1-s1, fieldwork notes; p1-s2, procedure 2.2].

**Recommendation.** Make the Branch Operations Manager signature a mandatory field in the account opening system so that an application without it cannot be activated, closing the gap where the system currently allows activation without the signature scanned in [p1-s2, fieldwork notes], and recheck the four affected accounts [p1-s1, fieldwork notes].

Note: the notes record that the branch manager agreed to fix the issue and wants 30 days [p1-s2, fieldwork notes]; I have not written that into the recommendation since it is an assurance, not a control — let me know if you want it included.

AAT103c-programme.need: Suggest programme steps from the library and past work

turns.asked: Suggest audit programme steps for the transaction profile process, drawing on our library and previous engagements. Say where each step comes from.
turns.answer:
Suggested steps for the transaction profile process

1. **Tie out the population.** Obtain the list of accounts opened in the period and agree the count to the system report.
   *From the 2025 audit programme, Step 1.*

2. **Test that a profile was recorded before activation.** Select a sample of accounts and inspect the application and system data to confirm a transaction profile was in place before the account was activated. This directly tests procedure 3.2 (no profile, no activation) and 3.1 (CSO records the declared amount).
   *Programme Step 3; procedure 3.1–3.2.*

3. **Verify the over-profile report and its reviews.** Obtain the monthly reports of accounts whose actual transactions exceeded the declared profile by more than 50% and confirm a review outcome was recorded for each, per procedure 3.3.
   *Programme Step 4; procedure 3.3.*

4. **Reperform the over-profile report.** Recalculate the report for one month straight from transaction data and compare it to the report the Compliance Officer reviewed, to test the report's completeness and accuracy.
   *Programme Step 5.*

5. **Test the dormancy/reactivation link (optional extension).** For dormant accounts (12 months without customer transaction, procedure 5.1), test that reactivation was reviewed, since procedure 5.2 flags unauthorised-staff-use risk.
   *Procedure 5.1–5.2; not in the 2025 programme, so I am adding it from the procedure text.*

6. **Align testing frequency to the requirement.** Procedure 6.2 requires Internal Audit to test a sample of new accounts every quarter; make sure the programme runs on that cadence.
   *Procedure 6.2.*

AAT104-rule.need: Plain-language test to a proposed rule, a sample run, then approval and reuse

turns.asked: I want to list all accounts opened in the last quarter (July to September 2026) where the transaction profile was not obtained, or where actual transactions in any month exceed the declared monthly amount by more than 50 percent. First propose the rule: name the files and fields you will use and explain the logic in plain language. Do not run it yet.
turns.answer:
## Proposed rule — "Q3 2026 account review"

**Files & fields**

| File | Fields used |
|---|---|
| `inputs/sample-accounts.csv` | `account_id`, `opened_on`, `profile_obtained`, `declared_monthly_amount` |
| `inputs/sample-transactions.csv` | `account_id`, `posted_on`, `amount` |

**Logic in plain language**

1. **Scope — accounts opened in Q3 2026.** From `sample-accounts.csv`, keep only rows where `opened_on` is on or after `2026-07-01` and on or before `2026-09-30`. (Inclusive on both ends.)
2. **Monthly actual turnover.** From `sample-transactions.csv`, for each `account_id` in the scope, sum `amount` for each calendar month in July, August and September 2026, using the month of `posted_on`. Only these three months are considered.
3. **Test A — profile not obtained.** Flag the account if `profile_obtained` is not `Y` (i.e. `N` or blank).

turns.answer:
ACME Information Security Policy (v1.0) — पाँच बिंदुओं में सारांश:

1. **लक्ष्य और दायरा** — यह नीति ACME की जानकारी और सिस्टम के लिए न्यूनतम सुरक्षा नियंत्रणों को तय करती है; उत्पादन, कॉर्पोरेट और ग्राहक-डेटा वातावरणों तक लागू है, और हर कर्मचारी, कॉन्ट्रैक्टर व सिस्टम पर लागू है [p1-s0 p.1] [p1-s1 p.1]।

2. **पहुँच (Access) नियंत्रण** — सिस्टम पहुँच न्यूनतम-अधिकार (least-privilege) आधार पर मिलती है, हर उपयोगकर्ता का अलग खाता (साझा खाते मना) है, पासवर्ड कम-से-कम 12 अक्षरों का, 12 महीने में पहुँच पुनरीक्षण, और निकलने के 5 कार्यदिवसों के भीतर पहुँच हटा दी जाती है [p1-s2 p.1]।

3. **एन्क्रिप्शन** — ग्राहक-डेटा पर AES-256 से एट-रस्ट एन्क्रिप्शन, सार्वजनिक नेटवर्क पर TLS 1.2+ एन्क्रिप्शन, और एन्क्रिप्शन कुंजियाँ हर साल रोटेट होती हैं [p1-s3 p.1]।

4. **लॉगिंग व नज़रबंदी** — प्रोडक्शन सिस्टम सेंट्रल लॉग प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर सिक्योरिटी लॉग भेजते हैं, लॉग 90 दिनों तक रखे जाते हैं, और सिक्योरिटी टीम कार्यदिवसों पर अलर्ट देखती है [p1-s4 p.1]।

5. **वेनडर, आईнциडेंट व बैकअप** — ग्राहक-डेटा संभालने वाले वेनडर से सौदे से पहले सिक्योरिटी सurvey में पूछताछ होती है; संदिग्ध आईнциडेंट को 24 घंटे में रिपोर्ट, सिखाए गए व्यक्तिगत-डेटा ब्रीच में प्रभावित ग्राहकों को 72 घंटे में सूचना, और प्रोडक्शन डेटाबेस का डेली बैकअप 30 दिनों तक [p1-s5 p.1] [p1-s6 p.1] [p1-s7 p.1]।

**अपवाद (Exceptions)** — नीति से अपवाद के लिए CISO की लिखित मंज़ूरी जरूरी है, और वह छह महीनों में ख़त्म हो जाती है [p1-s8 p.1]।
